newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nearly half of Finns oppose EMU membership - poll.
newsitem.headline: Nearly half of Finns oppose EMU membership - poll.

text.p: Finns opposed to membership of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) outnumber those in favour, according to an opinion poll released on Wednesday.
The survey said 45 percent opposed EMU while 36 percent supported Finnish participation in the single currency. About one fifth were undecided.
The opinion poll was made by research institute Taloustutkimus Oy among 1,924 Finns in November-December 1996.
The survey was made on behalf of Eurooppalainen Suomi, a pro-EU association. It said citizens in southern Finland were more pro-EMU than those in northern parts of the country. @

Half of business executives and other people in leading positions were in favour of EMU while 32 percent were opposed, of lower-level white-collar employees 42 percent said yes to EMU and 39 percent no, while 51 percent of blue-collar workers opposed and 29 percent supported EMU.

Among the unemployed, 52 percent oppose and 28 percent support EMU, among pensioners 50 percent were against and 31 percent in favour while 41 percent of students backed the single currency with 38 percent taking the opposite view.
With 42 percent for and 41 percent against men were more pro-EMU than women (48 percent against, 29 percent in favour). @
Among those under 24 years of age 40 percent supported EMU and 40 percent were against and in the 50-74 years age bracket 33 percent were pro-EMU while 47 percent opposed.
